newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S-E-Banken CEO changes refuels merger talk - papers.
newsitem.headline: S-E-Banken CEO changes refuels merger talk - papers.

text.p: A change of guard at Sweden's S-E-Banken prompted renewed speculation about a merger, possibly with Sweden's Nordbanken, in Swedish newspapers on Wednesday.

The bank announced on Tuesday that chief executive Bjorn Svedberg, 59, will step down next month and will be replaced by his current deputy, Jacob Wallenberg, 41, a member of the powerful Wallenberg family that holds a large stake in the bank.

"The reason Bjorn Svedberg, who brought S-E-Banken out of its deepest crisis, is now leaving the bank is that its owners, the Wallengbergs, think he is not the right person to lead the continuing restructuring," said business daily Dagens Industri.
Another Swedish financial paper, Finanstidningen, said the change in leadership signalled that a merger with state-controlled Nordbanken was back on the cards again.
Merger talks between the two banks collapsed in early February. Analysts speculated the reason talks broke down was related to a disagreement over future management.
"Tuesday's change in leadership...sends signals that a deal between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken could come about," Finanstidningen said.
"It was to a large extent Svedberg who opposed this deal and when Svedberg disappears, the obstacle to a merger also disappears."

According to Dagens Nyheter, in the negotiations with Nordbanken Svedberg has insisted he take the role of chairman, something which was not backed by the Wallenberg family and its investment vehicle Investor.
Jacob Wallenberg's task would be to lead the bank into a new structural deal, said Dagens Nyheter.

Sydsvenska Dagbladet said Svedberg had done all he could to bring about the merger but said he was disappointed about the way the Wallenbergs, who control about 18 percent of S-E-Banken, acted in connection with the talks.
Svedberg will leave the position of chairman after nearly five years at the bank's annual general meeting on April 29.
Wallenberg, the son of Peter Wallenberg who heads the family, has been with the bank, except for one short break, since 1984.
